result.topic_en: Diary entries (entries 113–119 of Gauss's mathematical diary, 1800–1801) recording methods for the class number of binary quadratic forms, the impossibility of reducing circle division to lower-degree equations, the date of Jewish Passover, a fifth proof of the fundamental theorem (quadratic reciprocity) via Gauss sums, a new method for computing orbital elements, and the start of lunar theory.
result.transcription:
Nov. 30, Felix fuit dies quo multitudinem
classium formarum binar. per triplicem methodum
assignare largitum est nobis puta 1) per prod. infin.
2) per aggregatum infinitum 3) per aggregatum fini-
tum cotangentium seu logarithm. sinuum. Brun.
# Dec. 3. Methodum quartam {+ex+} omnibus simplicissimam
deteximus pro dett. negativis ex sola multit. nume-
rorum $\varsigma, \varsigma'$ etc. petitam si $Ax+\varsigma$, $Ax+\varsigma'$ etc. sunt
formae lineares divisorum ${}^{\prime}\!\square + D$.          Ibid.
# Impossibile esse ut sectio circuli ad aequationes inferi-
ores quam theoria nostra suggerit reducatur demon-
stratum                    Brunov. Apr. 6
Iisdem diebus Pascha Iudaeorum per methodum novam
determinare docuimus (Apr. 1)
* Methodus quinta theorema fundamentale demonstrandi
se obtulit adiumento theorematis elegantissimi theoriae sectionis circuli
                         puta
$\Sigma \begin{matrix}\sin\\ \cos\end{matrix}\Big\} \frac{nn}{a}P = \begin{matrix}+\sqrt{a}\\+\sqrt{a}\end{matrix}\Big| \begin{matrix}0\\+\sqrt{a}\end{matrix}\Big| \begin{matrix}0\\0\end{matrix}\Big| \begin{matrix}+\sqrt{a}\\0\end{matrix}$ | substituendo pro n
prout $a \equiv 0 \quad 1 \quad 2 \quad 3 \pmod{4}$ | omnes numeros
                                   a 0 usque ad a-1
                         Brunsv. Mai. medio
# Methodus nova simplicissima expeditissi-
ma [-moti-] elementa orbitarum corporum coele-
stium investigandi.          Brunsv. Sept. m[?]
# Theoriam motus Lunae aggressi sumus Aug.
